keyTerms.definition: The map of the 15-week, 73-lab sequence.
Volumes 17 through 27; each category owns one volume.

recall.question: What does each week chapter list?
recall.answer: Every lab day, linked to the full walkthrough on its category page, with difficulty and task count at a glance.

keyTerms.definition: Labs rated Easy, Medium, Hard, or Expert per week.
The number above each bar; the x-axis is the week number.

recall.question: What does each bar show?
recall.answer: One week of the 15-week sequence; the number above is the lab count, the color is the difficulty mix.

keyTerms.definition: Exploratory data analysis: probe a dataset with plots and summaries before modeling.
NumPy, pandas, EDA; tools never become the bottleneck.

recall.question: Why does this week exist?
recall.answer: So tools never become the bottleneck; every later lab assumes you can load, slice, and check shapes without thinking.

sections.title: Week 2: The math you will actually use

keyTerms.definition: The direction of steepest change; training uses gradients to improve the model.
For uncertainty; with statistics for reading results.

recall.question: Why does math sit in week 2?
recall.answer: Because weeks 3 through 5 spend this math every day.

recall.question: Which pairing do interview questions combine most?
recall.answer: Linear algebra with probability, in the final math lab.

keyTerms.definition: Logistic regression teaches gradient-based fitting and convexity.
Generalized linear models, introduced via linear regression.

recall.question: Why do classical models come before neural networks?
recall.answer: Problems are small enough that every step is inspectable.

keyTerms.definition: The ways models break in practice; day 4 is the most interview-relevant day.
Day 5 combines the two weeks of models.

recall.question: Which day is the most interview-relevant?
recall.answer: Day 4, the classical ML failure modes lab.

keyTerms.definition: The week that separates people who train models from people who can tell whether a model is good.
Systematic debugging and error analysis after evaluation.

recall.question: Where do interviewers live?
recall.answer: In this week: evaluation and debugging questions appear in almost every ML loop.

keyTerms.definition: Computes gradients through a network's layers so training is possible.
The last Medium week; the on-ramp to the Hard block.

recall.question: What opens the bridge week?
recall.answer: Data preprocessing pipelines and data engineering, the unglamorous half of deep learning.

keyTerms.definition: The architecture family that made deep vision practical.
Methods that explain how training actually converges.

recall.question: What do activations and initialization explain?
recall.answer: How signals survive through layers; optimization explains how training converges.

sections.title: Week 8: CNNs in practice, then text

keyTerms.definition: Full image-classification lab using a frozen backbone.
To text: you cannot model sequences without first turning text into numbers.

recall.question: Why does the week pivot to text?
recall.answer: Week 9 starts sequence modeling, and you cannot model sequences without turning text into numbers first.

keyTerms.definition: Lets a model weigh which other positions matter for each position.
Learnable vector representations for words and items.

recall.question: What is day 5?
recall.answer: Self-attention, introduced after the RNN/LSTM history and the vectorized softmax craft.

keyTerms.definition: Generates text one token at a time, each conditioned on the ones before.
Six labs, 47 tasks, all Hard.

recall.question: What do you have by Friday?
recall.answer: A tiny autoregressive language model you built and trained.

keyTerms.definition: Retrieval-augmented generation: external documents at query time instead of only weights.
Library for fast approximate nearest-neighbor search over vectors.

recall.question: What is the shift this week?
recall.answer: From training models to building systems that use them.

keyTerms.definition: Pipelines, CI/CD, registries, monitoring, scaling, deployment.
Continuous integration and delivery: automated testing and deployment.

recall.question: What do interviewers test in this week?
recall.answer: Whether you think like an engineer who ships.

keyTerms.definition: Reason about tradeoffs at scale and defend choices; no single right answer.
Patterns for serving features; canonical design topic.

recall.question: When do design interviews begin?
recall.answer: Week 13: fundamentals, feature stores, real-time vs batch, recs/search/ads cases.

keyTerms.definition: The scaling-training lab bridges to the GPU and systems volumes.
Full real-time home feed recommender design.

recall.question: What does this week pair with?
recall.answer: Distributed training and inference-serving interview rounds.

keyTerms.definition: A system that uses a language model to plan and take actions, not just generate text.
Everything from fourteen weeks converges here.

recall.question: What converges in the capstone week?
recall.answer: Transformers from week 10, RAG from 11, serving from 12, design from 13-14.

keyTerms.definition: Each week block clears specific interview rounds; study matching weeks per round.
Mapped to rounds (a) through (h) with arrows.

recall.question: Which weeks clear the post-training deep dive and paper discussion?
recall.answer: Weeks 7 through 11.

recall.question: What clears the behavioral round?
recall.answer: All 15 weeks; every lab gives you a story about what broke.
